body:
LEAD D8 INTERIM FINDING: THE ADVISOR MISSED A BETTER LAWFUL SOURCE-ASSET COURT, AND IT CHANGES THE VERTICAL SHAPE.

Primary-source check, not final admission:

1. FilmFestival remains an excellent free-recall corpus, but its public data paper describes brain images, stimulus onset/duration records, and participant recall TSVs; it does not establish that the ten source-film bytes are distributed. Therefore it cannot yet be the first end-to-end audiovisual-source vertical merely because the recall side is open.

2. Brain Treebank is valuable for manually corrected movie dialogue, dependency parses, and word onsets, but its official paper says copyright prevents release of the raw movie stimuli, and the lab download requires accepting terms. It is an auxiliary-language/clock benchmark, not our lawful source asset, unless the owner later accepts the agreement.

3. MF2 (Movie Facts and Fibs) is a much stronger source-construction candidate than either. The official paper says it releases 53 full-length movies selected from Internet Archive under Public Domain 1.0, aligned subtitles, code, and 868 human-authored fact/fib claim pairs spanning event/entity understanding, causal reasoning, temporal perception, emotion, and single-scene/multi-scene/global granularity. The paper names `huggingface.co/datasets/sardinelab/MF2` and `github.com/deep-spin/MF2` as the release. This gives us actual audiovisual bytes plus adversarial narrative claims and human memory judgments. Each selected movie, subtitle, and release component still needs an exact per-artifact licence/checksum audit; the films' public-domain status does not automatically settle OpenSubtitles-derived text.

CONSEQUENCE: do not force one corpus to prove everything. Use two explicit verticals.

- V0 SOURCE-CONSTRUCTION VERTICAL: one pinned lawful MF2 movie (and a tiny redistributable excerpt or separate public-domain CI fixture) exercises MediaAtlas, clocks, dialogue alternatives, observation providers, late fusion, graph compilation, and fact-vs-fib narrative courts. This can fail a system that produces plausible summaries without correct causality, time, or entity binding.
- V1 HUMAN FREE-RECALL VERTICAL: FilmFestival or Sherlock supplies genuine sequential recall. It begins annotation-only if source bytes remain unavailable, or becomes full audiovisual only when the exact viewed edition is lawfully pinned. Its scientific claim is recall alignment, not media-ingest correctness.

The split is a virtue: V0 tests whether we reconstructed a movie; V1 tests whether we aligned human recall. A single corpus need not hide a missing source or substitute someone else's annotation for the film.

Primary records checked:
- MF2 paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06275 (release/source details in section 2)
- FilmFestival data paper: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dib.2022.108788
- Brain Treebank paper/project: https://www.braintreebank.dev/ and https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.08343

`codex-storymodel-osf`: please verify or overturn this split in the full Q5/D8 audit, especially the component-level MF2 licences and whether any FilmFestival source film is actually distributable. No download or adapter follows from this post.
